section: National - new central schemes, missions and their features
subsections: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion
Regional and rural development programmes → region + components
Scheme outlay and funding - outlay, period, external partner
Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose

accepted.s:
With reference to the launch of major national programmes, consider the following pairs:

Programme — Date of launch
1. Make in India — 25 September 2014
2. Digital India — 1 July 2015
3. Startup India — 16 January 2016
4. SVAMITVA — 24 April 2020

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Make in India, Digital India, Startup India and SVAMITVA were launched on 25 September 2014, 1 July 2015, 16 January 2016 and 24 April 2020, respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each date with the programme before eliminating the coded options.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 by which institution?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
accepted.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The programme is structured around nine pillars.
accepted.tq: Use the agency-purpose association to distinguish neighbouring technology departments.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020 on the occasion of:
accepted.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020 on National Panchayati Raj Day.
accepted.tq: Link the launch date with the specific commemorative occasion.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their launch:
A. Make in India
B. Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan
C. Startup India
D. SVAMITVA
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Make in India (2014), Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (2015), Startup India (2016) and SVAMITVA (2020).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two intervening programmes.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Gyan Bharatam Mission is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: The Gyan Bharatam Mission, announced in July 2025, focuses on manuscript digitisation. Its National Manuscript Survey began in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact purpose instead of choosing a broadly related digitisation activity.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The AP cluster centre of the Gyan Bharatam Mission is run by:
accepted.x: The AP cluster centre of Gyan Bharatam is run by the Sanatana Jeevan Trust and deals particularly with palm-leaf manuscripts.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-purpose association to identify the correct implementing institution.
accepted.sec: Launch chronology → year, launched by, occasion  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Vibrant Villages Programme-I?
o: A Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering 46 blocks in 19 districts along the northern border
A Central Sector Scheme covering all international border villages from 2024–25 to 2028–29
A State-funded scheme covering coastal villages only
A scheme restricted to villages in the North-Eastern States
accepted.x: Vibrant Villages Programme-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering 46 blocks in 19 districts along the northern border, including areas in Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh.
accepted.tq: Separate the scheme’s classification, coverage and geography from those of its later version.
accepted.sec: Regional and rural development programmes → region + components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers villages on:
o: The coastline of the eastern States
The inter-State boundaries of the North-East
accepted.x: VVP-II, implemented from 2024–25 to 2028–29, covers villages on other international land borders. It is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the northern-border focus of VVP-I and the other land borders under VVP-II.
accepted.sec: Regional and rural development programmes → region + components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: VVP-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, whereas VVP-II is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding. Therefore, VVP-I and 100% central funding are not correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped feature between the two similarly named programmes.
accepted.sec: Regional and rural development programmes → region + components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The SPM Rurban Mission provides for population clusters of:
o: 25,000–50,000 in plains/coastal areas and 5,000–25,000 in desert, hilly and tribal areas
10,000–20,000 in plains and 20,000–40,000 in hilly areas
5,000–25,000 in plains/coastal areas and 25,000–50,000 in desert areas
accepted.x: The SPM Rurban Mission covers clusters of 25,000–50,000 people in plains and coastal areas, and 5,000–25,000 people in desert, hilly and tribal areas.
accepted.tq: Check the reversed population ranges and geographical conditions carefully.
accepted.sec: Regional and rural development programmes → region + components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The SPM Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is funded mainly through:
o: A dedicated cess on rural property
accepted.x: The SPM Rurban Mission was launched in 2016 and is funded through convergence of different schemes. It envisages more than 300 clusters.
accepted.tq: Identify the funding mechanism rather than the numerical coverage.
accepted.sec: Regional and rural development programmes → region + components  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sampada, a platform for e-registration of property, is associated with which State?
accepted.x: Sampada is the Madhya Pradesh platform for e-registration of property.
accepted.tq: Pair the platform with its State rather than with a similarly named land-record service.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Platform — Purpose
1. DigiLocker — Cloud-based storage of documents
2. e-Shram — National database of unorganised workers
3. e-Jagriti — Online consumer complaints
4. Mana Mitra — WhatsApp governance service in Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. DigiLocker provides cloud documents, e-Shram maintains the database of unorganised workers, e-Jagriti handles consumer complaints and Mana Mitra provides WhatsApp governance services in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure platform-purpose pairs and verify the State-specific service last.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: DigiLocker documents are recognised as valid under:
o: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, Rule 5
The Representation of the People Act, Section 9A
accepted.x: DigiLocker documents have legal validity under Rule 9A of the Information Technology Rules. DigiLocker was launched in 2015 by MeitY.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact rule number from similar statutory section numbers.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The e-Shram portal provides which of the following for unorganised workers?
accepted.x: e-Shram, launched in August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, creates a national database of unorganised workers and provides a 12-digit UAN.
accepted.tq: Use the number-format clue to distinguish the worker database identifier from other government numbers.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sujal Gaon ID under Sujalam Bharat is intended to provide:
o: A land title number for rural properties
A digital identity for each rural water supply scheme
A digital identity for every urban household
A subsidy code for LPG consumers
accepted.x: Sujal Gaon ID provides a digital identity for each rural water scheme under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. It is associated with the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
accepted.tq: Infer the service from the rural-water context and reject unrelated identity systems.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PM-AJAY Portal and AJAY app are associated with which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
accepted.x: The PM-AJAY Portal and AJAY app are associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and aim to make PM-AJAY paperless.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which Ministry’ trap to distinguish closely related welfare departments.
accepted.sec: Digital platforms/portals/apps → agency/state + purpose  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-SETU for ITI upgradation:
1. Its total outlay is ₹60,000 crore over five years.
2. The Centre, States and industry contribute ₹30,000 crore, ₹20,000 crore and ₹10,000 crore respectively.
3. The World Bank and ADB co-finance 50% of the central share.
4. It covers 1,000 ITIs in hub-and-spoke clusters.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. PM-SETU has a ₹60,000 crore five-year outlay, the stated Centre-State-industry sharing pattern, multilateral co-financing of half the central share and coverage of 1,000 ITIs.
accepted.tq: Break the scheme into outlay, contribution, external partner and coverage before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Scheme outlay and funding - outlay, period, external partner  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following schemes is identified as World Bank-aided and intended for minority youth?
accepted.x: Nai Manzil is a World Bank-aided programme intended for minority youth. Atal Bhujal Yojana is also listed among World Bank-aided schemes, but has a different focus.
accepted.tq: Separate schemes sharing the same external partner by their target group and purpose.
accepted.sec: Scheme outlay and funding - outlay, period, external partner  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The revised outlay for PM-KISAN up to 2030–31 is:
accepted.x: PM-KISAN has been extended up to 2030–31 with an outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Read the lakh-crore figure precisely and eliminate options differing by one digit.
accepted.sec: Scheme outlay and funding - outlay, period, external partner  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: SASCI provides States with:
o: Foreign exchange loans for private infrastructure projects
Ten-year interest-bearing revenue loans within the 3% deficit cap
50-year interest-free capital expenditure loans outside the 3% deficit cap
accepted.x: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans to States for capital expenditure. These loans are outside the 3% fiscal deficit cap.
accepted.tq: Identify both the purpose and the exceptional fiscal treatment in the applied description.
accepted.sec: Scheme outlay and funding - outlay, period, external partner  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: ULLAS, also known as Nav Bharat Saksharta, primarily targets:
o: Adult literacy among persons aged 15 years and above
Digital literacy among children below six years
accepted.x: ULLAS is the adult literacy programme for persons aged 15 years and above, with the slogan ‘Jan Jan Sakshar’. Its outlay is ₹1,037.90 crore for 2022–27.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its age group and educational objective.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM SHRI — Collateral-free higher education loans
DIKSHA — Digital content for school teaching
accepted.x: PM SHRI is a programme for developing more than 14,500 model schools aligned with NEP. Collateral-free education loans are associated with PM Vidyalaxmi.
accepted.tq: Find the purpose swapped between two education schemes.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Skills Qualifications Framework is primarily concerned with:
o: Providing direct cash transfers to trainees
accepted.x: NSQF establishes competency-based qualification levels. Care-giver training is also aligned with the framework.
accepted.tq: Choose the definition that states what the framework measures rather than an associated activity.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PM SHRI schools are intended to be:
o: Residential schools exclusively for tribal children
More than 14,500 model schools aligned with NEP
accepted.x: PM SHRI aims to develop more than 14,500 model schools aligned with the National Education Policy. The implementation period is 2022–23 to 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Use the scale and model-school objective to distinguish PM SHRI from other education initiatives.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PM Vidyalaxmi, launched in November 2024, provides:
accepted.x: PM Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free education loans. The number of covered institutions has subsequently reached 1,425.
accepted.tq: Distinguish student-finance support from school-improvement and State-capital schemes.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the first Union Territory to become fully literate under ULLAS?
accepted.x: Ladakh became the first Union Territory to become fully literate under ULLAS in 2024. The benchmark for being declared fully literate is 95% literacy.
accepted.tq: Separate the first Union Territory from the first State in the ULLAS sequence.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The literacy threshold used for declaring an area fully literate under ULLAS is:
accepted.x: The benchmark for being declared fully literate under ULLAS is 95% literacy; complete 100% literacy is not required.
accepted.tq: Reject the attractive but excessive ‘100 percent’ threshold.
accepted.sec: Education and skill programmes → ministry + purpose  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under PAHAL, the LPG subsidy is transferred when:
o: The subsidy is credited to the gas agency before delivery
The consumer pays a subsidised price and receives no subsequent transfer
The consumer receives the cylinder free of cost from the distributor
The consumer buys the cylinder at market price and the subsidy is credited to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account
accepted.x: Under PAHAL, the LPG cylinder is bought at market price and the subsidy is subsequently credited to the consumer’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
accepted.tq: Trace the sequence of purchase, subsidy credit and bank-account linkage.
accepted.sec: DBT and subsidy reform → mechanism  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The JAM trinity, which forms the base of Direct Benefit Transfer, consists of:
accepted.x: JAM stands for Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile. The idea was set out in the Economic Survey 2014–15 and became the foundation for DBT delivery.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym exactly and avoid replacing one of its three components with a policy objective.
accepted.sec: DBT and subsidy reform → mechanism  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: CBDC-based DBT involves payment of subsidy through:
accepted.x: Under CBDC-based DBT, the subsidy is paid as a programmable digital rupee. This mechanism was introduced in 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the payment instrument and distinguish it from conventional bank-account DBT.
accepted.sec: DBT and subsidy reform → mechanism  [other exams, GROUP-II]
